messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: p99 latency SLO burn for service="inference-api" region="eu-west" (threshold=1200ms). Current p99=1890ms. page: PD-INC-10234
Maya: acked. I am on it, grabbing metrics and checking autoscaler.
Maya: quick note - suspected traffic spike to kv-cache-backed endpoints (chat-history reranks).
Oliver: Maya — can you paste the p95/p99 times and rps snapshot? also which model routes are hot?
Maya: metrics snapshot:
```
window: 15m
rps: 320 -> 420
p95: 420ms
p99: 1890ms
kvcache_hit_rate: 21% (normally ~72%)
active_workers: 64 -> 64 (no autoscale events)
queue_depth: 120 -> 240
```
Maya: looks like KV cache thrash and queueing on hotside. no autoscaler scale-up observed — check control plane logs.
Lee: checking autoscaler logs and GPU pool health now. running: `kubectl -n inference get hpa,deploy -l pool=eu-west`
Lee: autoscaler logs show throttle on controller due to missing quota call to cloud account. snippet:
```
2026-03-14T10:16:32Z controller: scale request denied: quotaCheck failed: API 429
2026-03-14T10:16:35Z controller: backoff applied
```
Lee: quota burst blocked scale up. Eng-Infra alert already opened (INFRA-731).
Maya: can we shift some traffic to dedicated pool (eu-west-dedicated) or fallback to smaller quantized model to reduce token compute?
Sam: product here — we have two enterprise customers on affected routes (AcmeCorp, BeaconHealth). Jess from CS, any immediate customer reports?
Jess: AcmeCorp reported timeouts in last 5m, support ticket created. BeaconHealth hasn't reported but we should proactively notify.
Oliver: mitigation plan suggestion: (1) temporarily route 35% of traffic for route=/v1/chat to dedicated pool eu-west-dedicated; (2) enable fallback to model `redwood/gpt-medium-q4` for low-latency tier; (3) warm KV cache for top 10 prefixes; (4) request quick quota bump.
Maya: doing step 1 now — running routing change via console API:
```
# shift 35% to dedicated pool
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.internal/routing/shift -d '{"route":"/v1/chat","from":"shared-eu-west","to":"eu-west-dedicated","pct":35}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```
Maya: API accepted, confirming traffic shift starting.
incident-bot: :information_source: Routing change applied: shiftId=sh-20260314-01 state=rolling (35% -> eu-west-dedicated).
Maya: enabling fallback model policy for /v1/chat to use `redwood/gpt-medium-q4` when latency > 800ms.
Oliver: I'll prepare a canary rollback for the most expensive model variant on that route — command: `deployctl rollback model gpt-large-20260301 --route /v1/chat --canary 20`
Lee: autoscaler controller team responded — they are applying an emergency quota override with cloud infra. ETA ~4m.
Anya: I'm paged as SRE lead for escalation. If quota override fails, prepare capacity shedding policy: reduce per-request max_tokens to 512 and throttle burst windows for non-critical tenants.
Sam: agree. Sam -> product will mark AcmeCorp as high-priority and coordinate with CS for incident comms.
Jess: sending AcmeCorp a short note now: "We're investigating increased latency in EU, shifting traffic and enabling fallbacks. We'll follow up." :white_check_mark:
Maya: KV cache warmup in progress for top prefixes (k=10). warming script logs:
```
warm: prefix=\"/convo/1234\" status=ok
warm: prefix=\"/convo/9876\" status=ok
warm: done 10/10
```
Maya: observed immediate p99 drop to ~980ms after routing shift + fallbacks. still above SLO but improving.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-INC-10234 acknowledged by Maya. Escalation to Anya at 10:23 UTC.
Oliver: monitoring heatmap — model gpt-large pods still showing high tail latency. I'll throttle new session creation on that variant: `curl -X POST /internal/limit -d '{"model":"gpt-large","new_sessions":false}'`
Maya: executed. new sessions blocked for gpt-large. existing in-flight complete.
Anya: request logs from the router for contested requests: `routerctl tail --region eu-west --filter "route:/v1/chat status:queued" | head`
Anya: looking at results — a small percentage of legacy clients still hitting shared pool. sending a 302 to them to prefer dedicated endpoint.
Maya: applied 302 for legacy client user-agent pattern `LegacySDK/1.*`.
Lee: autoscaler override succeeded from infra, controller reports scale to 96 workers. provisioning in progress.
Maya: once workers spin up, we should see p99 drop under 600ms. keeping canary and throttle in place until stable.
Maya: handoff: I'm going offline in ~20m for another incident response. handing to Oliver for steady-state monitoring. Oliver, you have the incident.
Oliver: taking over. summary for next oncall: routing shift 35%, fallback model gpt-medium-q4 enabled, gpt-large new sessions blocked, autoscaler override applied (target 96), KV cache warmed. watch p99 and queue_depth.
Anya: assigned follow-up action items: (1) postmortem owner=Oliver; (2) infra to confirm quota root cause; (3) eng-runtime to add circuit-breaker for kv-cache thrash.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: PagerDuty: PD-INC-10234 resolved (ack -> resolved) at 10:48 UTC. final metrics snapshot:
```
window: 30m
rps: stabilized 340
p95: 380ms
p99: 520ms
kvcache_hit_rate: 68%
active_workers: 96
queue_depth: 12
```
Maya: thanks team. I'll draft the incident summary. Oliver, please own the postmortem.
Oliver: will do. I'll include timeline, mitigation steps, and recommend autoscaler resiliency improvements.
Sam: I'll coordinate customer comms and send an update to AcmeCorp and BeaconHealth.
Jess: follow-up note sent to AcmeCorp: "Service restored; we're performing root cause analysis and will share a postmortem soon."
Anya: :thumbsup: good job. Closing channel after postmortem created.
